notable_absence.finding: This is the richest privilege matrix found in this batch: unlike every other statement here, the Advanced-credential privilege is keyed by BOTH credential type AND function scope (global vs. scoped) - two named Advanced privileges for one statement, not one. The Basic side stays a flat 'Write' regardless of scope, so the extra axis only exists on the Advanced side. This is a genuine structural variant on the round-2 disjunctive-pair hypothesis: it's not disjunctive here, it's a second orthogonal condition (scope) layered onto the credential-type condition.

cross_component_finding: Recurrence of the known issue docs-issues/capella-pages-cite-server-versions.json: the 'SQL++ Managed User-Defined Functions' section is headed 'Couchbase Server 7.6' and begins 'For operational clusters using Couchbase Server 7.6 and later, you can create the code for a JavaScript function and the corresponding SQL++ user-defined function in a single operation in the Query Tab or cbq.' Also notable: this same sentence refers to 'operational clusters,' a Capella-specific framing (implicitly contrasting with Capella's own serverless/other cluster types) layered on top of the server-version citation - suggesting the version gate may have originally applied only to a subset of Capella deployment types, not a straightforward server-version copy-paste.
